subject: Private VPC next steps / PrivateLink vs peering + egress IPs (AxiomPay POC)
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Park <sophie@axiompay.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private VPC next steps / PrivateLink vs peering + egress IPs (AxiomPay POC)

Hi Sophie — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a clear handoff between network/security and procurement: 

• Summary from our side: AxiomPay is leaning toward a Private VPC (PrivateLink) deployment for the POC to minimize internet egress and meet SOC-2 customer requirements. You mentioned 30–50 TPS expected at peak and a desire to keep model inference traffic inside your VPC.

• Immediate asks from Redwood to prepare a PrivateLink onboarding run:
  1) AxiomPay network diagram (VPC IDs, CIDR(s), subnets for endpoints) — attach if available.
  2) Preferred connectivity: PrivateLink (VPC endpoint) vs VPC Peering — you said PrivateLink preferred but open to validation.
  3) Egress/allowlist constraints: any existing company-wide IP allowlist patterns or static NAT egress IPs we should publish.
  4) Security questionnaire items: key rotation cadence, expected data residency controls, and whether a shared DNS (private zone) is acceptable.

Can you share the network diagram and the two-week availability window for a 30–45 minute deep-dive with our network engineer (karthik_iyer@redwood.com)? I’m CC’ing Aditya for procurement/contract questions and Marissa for onboarding coordination.

I’ve attached the call recording and will follow up with our PrivateLink runbook and a short checklist for the deep-dive.

Thanks — Irene

--
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

From: Sophie Park <sophie@axiompay.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@axiompay.com
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private VPC next steps / PrivateLink vs peering + egress IPs (AxiomPay POC)

Irene — thanks for the summary and for the fast turnaround. Confirming a few items from our side: 

1) Connectivity preference: PrivateLink. Our security team prefers endpoint-based access and wants traffic to never traverse the public internet.
2) Expected load: 30 TPS sustained, 50 TPS spikes (payloads small, typical token lengths ~75).
3) Timeline: POC target kickoff week of Jan 4.
4) Attachments: sharing our initial network diagram and security checklist (see attachments). Note the diagram is v1 — we will update with exact subnet IDs once infra team is back next week.

Attachments: axiom_network_diagram_v1.pdf; axiom_security_requirements.xlsx

We can do the network deep-dive on either Dec 18 (after 1pm PT) or Dec 20 (morning PT). Karthik — please let us know what you need (routes, NAT, endpoints, TLS certs).

Best,
Sophie
VP, Infrastructure | AxiomPay
[sophie@axiompay.com]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Park <sophie@axiompay.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private VPC next steps / PrivateLink vs peering + egress IPs (AxiomPay POC)

Thanks Sophie — looking at the diagram helped. For the run-of-show on the deep-dive, here are the concrete preflight items we need from AxiomPay and the values we’ll validate during the meeting: 

Preflight checklist (please provide where possible before the call):
- VPC ID(s) and exact CIDR(s) for endpoint placement (example: vpc-0a1b2c 10.0.0.0/16).
- Subnet IDs (private subnets) intended for the PrivateLink endpoints and route table names.
- Preferred PrivateLink DNS behavior: use private hosted zone (split-horizon) or explicit endpoint IPs?
- Any NAT/transit egress that will cause outbound traffic (we need to know if there are shared egress NAT IPs). If you have static egress IPs, please list them so we can publish allowlist entries.
- TLS termination preference: client side TLS to the endpoint, or will you terminate TLS at a load balancer and speak plaintext on internal network? We strongly recommend end-to-end TLS.
- IAM/service account that will create/own the VPC endpoint (ARN/email).
- Route53 private zone names if you plan to use private DNS (e.g., internal.redwood.axiompay.svc).
- Contact for on-call ops during the POC cutover (phone + email).

What Redwood will provide before the call:
- redwood_privatelink_runbook.pdf (attached) — includes sample CloudFormation/Terraform snippet and expected route entries.
- List of Redwood egress IPs used if peering fallback needed.
- Suggested monitoring template (CloudWatch + tracing tags) for the POC.

If Dec 18 after 1pm PT works for you Sophie, let’s lock 45 minutes and I’ll include a short validation checklist to go over live.

-karthik
Principal Network Engineer | Redwood Inference
[karthik_iyer@redwood.com]
[Attachment: redwood_privatelink_runbook.pdf]
